source.title: Discovering Chunks in Neural Embeddings for Interpretability
source.authors: Shu-Chen Wu; S. Alaniz; Eric Schulz; Zeynep Akata

record.tranche_reason: The authors argue that studying individual neurons alone is insufficient and develop population-level chunks as an alternative. Their experiments concern chunks, not the specific neuron-pole claims or tests named in the versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's own measurements concern recurring population-level activity chunks. It does not measure neuron-pole job counts, explanation accuracy on held-out activations, or the other specified version outcomes. Its discussion that monosemantic neurons are a small fraction is attributed to prior work and is not counted as a result here.
record.test_reason: The study proposes population-level 'chunk' extraction (discrete sequence chunking, population averaging, unsupervised dictionaries) in a 12-unit RNN and LLaMA3-8B. It never audits individual neuron poles, never scores neuron explanations on held-out text, and never builds neuron-level attribution graphs. Its statement that monosemantic neurons are a small fraction is a cited background claim from prior work, not a result. It neither tests nor uses the claim, so T6 rather than T5: it offers no specific argument or result that any version is wrong, only a motivating literature summary.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance: the authors conclude that recurring chunks exist in RNN and LLM neural dynamics, that chunking can segment high-dimensional activity into interpretable units whose perturbation alters behaviour, and they frame this as an initial proof of concept needing further testing and better extraction methods.
record.recipe_differences: The study extracts recurring population-activity chunks using discrete sequence chunking, population averaging, or unsupervised dictionaries, rather than auditing neuron poles or testing neuron explanations on held-out activations.
record.method_sensitivity: For population averaging, the authors report more faithful detection in earlier layers than later layers. They also note that averaging can be less identifiable where a signal has multiple contextual variants.

fits_no_version.finding: Population-averaged subpopulation chunks in LLaMA3-8B detect recurring words (cheese, cake, cheesecake) with high TPR and low FPR; earlier layers more faithful than later.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Word-specific neural subpopulation chunks are detectable across LLaMA3-8B layers, with fidelity declining in later layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Grafting or zeroing extracted chunks shifts RNN predictions and biases or suppresses topic words in LLaMA3-8B generation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Population-level chunks are causally relevant units that can steer or suppress concepts.

fits_no_version.finding: Trained RNN has more unique population states and recurring chunks than untrained; discrete trajectories decode inputs perfectly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training creates context-distinguishing population states in small RNNs.

fits_no_version.finding: Unsupervised chunks correlate strongly with POS tags across LLaMA layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unsupervised population chunks align with syntactic categories.

record.code_released: Software will be published conjunctively with paper; no URL stated.
record.problems: The LLM experiments use LLaMA3-8B only. The text gives qualitative descriptions rather than numerical rates for key LLM chunk-detection and intervention results. The authors describe the work as an initial proof of concept and identify limitations in chunk extraction.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported result relevant to the claim versions was left out. Figure-only numerical details were not transcribed where the text did not state the values.

Neuron-pole shares in other dense/MoE models and at scale.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron and recursive generalization vs superposition.
Effect of architecture, regularization and tools on share of interpretable neurons.
Neuron-based attribution graphs without replacement models.
Whether activating-example explanations predict firing on new text.
Simulation-based automated scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T5 to T6: the only neuron-level content is a literature summary (monosemantic neurons are 'a small fraction'), cited to prior work, which bears loosely on V1/V2 but is not the study's own result. No verdicts given. All rows correctly linked to 'none'. Appendix H's remark that prepositions yield less identifiable chunks is a chunk-method observation, not a neuron result.

versions.untested_parts: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole proportions and the proportion of poles not understood.
Shares of interpretable neuron poles across models, architectures, and scales.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron, pose, and recursive generalization.
Effects of architecture, regularization, or tools on neuron interpretability rates, including the InceptionV1-sized estimates.
Attribution graphs built from a large model's own neurons and their reconstruction error.
Whether explanations from activating examples predict firing on new examples.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.
